title: requirements.json — source-grounded obligations and their judgment responsibilities
description: Accounts for the delivered intent and its material context. Entries retain source wording and explicit responsibility; repeated statements can share an obligation. Readers consult the original sources to resolve meaning.

id.description: Unique in this file and stable for an unchanged obligation. Design and verification artifacts reference it; update affected references when entries are revised.

verbatim.description: Quoted source wording with the labels and context needed to preserve meaning. Interpretations and decisions belong in note rather than being presented as user wording.

judge.description: Who establishes this entry: a stage, a decision under the actual authorization (human), or an explicit responsibility outside this workflow (outside). none records context without a separate verification obligation. unassignable records unresolved treatment or necessary basis, explained in note, and prevents successful specification closure. Lack of an automatic parser does not by itself put an obligation outside; stages can judge other evidence.

target.description: A numerical bound in a dimension and unit supported by the judging stage. The computed verdict covers that quantity and measurement scope only; other independent obligations require their own judgment. Non-target obligations are judged from evidence by the responsible reader.

dim.description: Measurement dimension supported by the selected stage; that stage validates and interprets it.

op.description: The engineer's comparison, transcribed: actual op value must hold.

scenario.description: power_mw only: present when the engineer's bound names a power scenario.

note.description: Entry scope, source references, interpretation, decision and authorization basis, or the concrete unresolved issue. A note does not add obligations to an automatic numerical verdict.
